questiontext.text:
The diagram shows a regular {@poly@} on top of a square. Find angle \(x\) in degrees.

truefeedback.text:
Here is a worked solution:

\(x\) is the sum of the exterior angles of the square and {@poly@}.

To find the exterior angle of a polygon: \(\theta_{\mathsf{ext}} = \frac{360^\circ}{\mathsf{number\:of\:sides}}\)

Exterior angle of a square: \(\frac{360}{4} = 90^\circ\)

Exterior angle of a {@poly@}: \(\frac{360}{{@sides@}} = {@if sides=7 then dispdp(360/7,3) else 360/sides@}^\circ\)

Therefore, \(x = 90 + {@if sides=7 then dispdp(360/7,3) else 360/sides@} = {@sol@}^\circ\) {@if sides=7 then "to the nearest whole degree." else ""@}
You have found the sum of the interior angles as opposed to \(x\), the sum of the exterior angles.

The exact value of \(x\) is \(\frac{990}{7} = 141.4285...\)
Rounded to the nearest whole degree, this is \(141^\circ\).

You have attempted to find the sum of the interior angles as opposed to \(x\), the sum of the exterior angles.
The exact sum of the interior angles is \(\frac{1530}{7} = 218.5714...\)
Rounded to the nearest whole degree, this is \(219^\circ\).
